vrpentries.path: Full path of the file or link: index name first, then the path inside the index (e.g. myindex/dir/file.txt). Ordinary TEXT: filter with path LIKE 'myindex/dir/%', GROUP BY, etc. In aggregate_sql_query, to use path in partial_sql or final_sql, carry it through per_directory_shape and partial_shape.
vrpentries.dirpath: Full path of the directory containing the file or link (e.g. myindex/dir). Filter with dirpath LIKE 'myindex/dir/%'.
vrpentries.spath: Path on the source file system that was indexed (not the index-name-first form). For reference only; path filters use the path column.

vrsummary.path: Full path of the directory (e.g. myindex/dir; the index root is myindex). Index name first, then path inside the index. Filter with path LIKE 'myindex/sub/%'. In aggregate_sql_query, carry path through per_directory_shape and partial_shape to use it in later stages.
vrsummary.spath: Path on the source file system that was indexed (not the index-name-first form). For reference only; path filters use the path column.

vrsummarylong.path: Full path of the directory (e.g. myindex/dir; the index root is myindex). Index name first, then path inside the index. Filter with path LIKE 'myindex/sub/%'. In aggregate_sql_query, carry path through per_directory_shape and partial_shape to use it in later stages.
vrsummarylong.spath: Path on the source file system that was indexed (not the index-name-first form). For reference only; path filters use the path column.

bytecat.tag: bytecat({col}) -> size band (Zero, B, K, M, G, ...)
bytecat.detail: GUFI's standard size bands, 1024-based: Zero (0), B (<1K), K (<1M), M (<1G), G (<1T), T (<1P), P (<1E), E. Use it as the group key for a breakdown of files by size.
bytecat.example: SELECT bytecat(size) AS band, COUNT(*) AS n FROM entries GROUP BY band

human_readable_size.detail: Formats a byte count with one decimal and a 1024-based unit (K, M, G, T, P, E). For display only: apply it in final_sql to summed values, never group or sum on its output.

intcat.tag: intcat({col}) -> count band (Zero, O, K, M, B, ...)
intcat.detail: 1000-based bands for counts: Zero, O (<1000), K (<1 million), M (<1 billion), B (<1 trillion), T, q, Q. Use as a group key to bucket directories by how many entries they hold.
intcat.example: SELECT intcat(totfiles) AS band FROM vrsummary

agecat.tag: agecat({col}) -> age band (Secs, Mins, Hrs, Days, Wks, Mos, Yrs, Decs)
agecat.detail: GUFI's standard age bands, measured from the server's current clock (not a time you pass in): Zero, Secs (<1 min), Mins (<1 h), Hrs (<1 day), Days (<1 week), Wks (<30 days), Mos (<365 days), Yrs (<10 years), Decs. Use it as the group key for a breakdown by age. Errors on times in the future.
agecat.example: SELECT agecat(atime) AS band, COUNT(*) AS n FROM entries GROUP BY band

epochtoage.detail: Age from the server's current clock in whole units, rounded down. unit: 's' seconds, 'm' minutes, 'h' hours, 'd' days (default), 'w' weeks, 'M' months (30 days), 'y' years (365 days), 'D' decades. For cutoffs relative to a time you were given, compare the column with arithmetic on that time instead.
epochtoage.example: SELECT epochtoage(atime, 'w') AS weeks FROM entries

strftime.detail: C strftime(3) on an epoch, in the server's local time zone. Replaces SQLite's strftime, so the argument order is (format, epoch) and SQLite modifiers such as 'unixepoch' are not accepted. Useful as a group key by year or month.
strftime.example: SELECT strftime('%Y', ctime) AS year FROM entries

uidtouser.detail: Looks the uid up on the server host. Returns the number as text when the host has no such user. Group on uid and convert in final_sql, which does one lookup per uid instead of per file.
uidtouser.example: SELECT uidtouser(uid) AS owner, SUM(bytes) FROM partial GROUP BY uid

gidtogroup.detail: Looks the gid up on the server host. Returns the number as text when the host has no such group. Group on gid and convert in final_sql.
gidtogroup.example: SELECT gidtogroup(gid) AS grp, SUM(n) FROM partial GROUP BY gid

modetotxt.detail: ls-style permission string, including the file type character. For display; filter with integer bitmasks on mode instead.
modetotxt.example: SELECT modetotxt(mode) AS perms FROM entries

ext.tag: ext({col}) -> extension after the last dot, NULL if none
ext.detail: Text after the last '.' (without the dot): 'a.tar.gz' -> 'gz', '.bashrc' -> 'bashrc'. NULL when there is no dot or the name ends with one. Use it as the group key for a breakdown by extension.
ext.example: SELECT ext(name) AS e, COUNT(*) AS n FROM entries GROUP BY e

basename.detail: Last component of a path, ignoring trailing slashes. The name column already holds the basename of each entry.
basename.example: SELECT basename(dirpath) AS dir FROM vrpentries

median.detail: Median of a column. Medians cannot be combined across stages, so a median over the whole index needs every value carried into final_sql: per_directory_sql and partial_sql pass the raw values through and final_sql takes median(value) FROM partial. That row count can be large.

stdevs.detail: Sample standard deviation. Over the whole index, compute SUM(x * x), SUM(x) and COUNT(*) in the earlier stages, SUM each in final_sql, and finish with stdev_from_parts.

stdevp.detail: Population standard deviation. Combine across stages the same way as stdevs, with stdev_from_parts.

stdev_from_parts.signature: stdev_from_parts(sum_of_squares, sum, count, sample INT64) -> REAL
stdev_from_parts.detail: Standard deviation from summed parts, for final_sql. sample is 1 for sample and 0 for population standard deviation.
stdev_from_parts.example: SELECT stdev_from_parts(SUM(sq), SUM(s), SUM(n), 1) FROM partial

hostname.detail: Host name of the machine running gufi_query.

rpad.detail: Pads text with spaces to width. Used for gufi_ls and gufi_find output.

blocksize.detail: Block count in ls style, meant only for gufi_ls. Do not use it for sizes; use size, bytecat, or human_readable_size.
